partA.verdict: Moderate localized staleness: Herr Ott locked into Lesen T3 seeker slot in 10/15 files. Rest of titled cast is reasonably diverse (25 unique). Bare given-name hit counts are inflated by within-dialogue repetition, not cross-exam reuse.

codeAssignment.poolPersisted: Almost all pool questions still have integer difficulty (template/default).
codeAssignment.normalizeBatchDefaults: scripts/lib/normalizeBatch.mjs normalizeDifficulty: horen→5, sprechen→5, schreiben→6, else→4 when missing/invalid.
codeAssignment.stripPoolLegacyOptionB: stripPoolLegacyQuestionFields deletes difficulty for Lesen normalize path (Opción B 2026-07-10) so runtime DifficultyScorer can recompute — but current pool-verified JSON still contains persisted values.
codeAssignment.runtimeScorer: js/engine/validation/difficultyScorer.js scoreQuestion: if q.difficulty ∈ [1,10] SHORT-CIRCUITS and returns it; else scores via CefrGate metrics. So persisted pool values block recalculation.
codeAssignment.backlog: BACKLOG.md DIFF-SCORE / DIFF-POOL-RO — treat pool difficulty as non-authoritative.

partB.verdict: Decorative/template: only {4,5,6}, fixed per module (Lesen=4, Hören/Sprechen=5, Schreiben=6), never varies within a file. Not a per-question measurement. Runtime DifficultyScorer exists but is short-circuited when pool value present; Opción B intends strip+runtime but pool still largely stamped.
